output.summary: About 73% of the shrink increase sits in DSD categories. It follows the April 2025 removal of receiving clerks: no-clerk stores went from 1.4% to 3.0% shrink and clerk stores to 1.7%. The August audit found invoiced value exceeding counted value by 4.9%. A matched-control pilot cut DSD shrink from 4.4% to 1.9%, and receiver labor cost far less than the credits recovered. External theft, associate theft and the count-firm change do not explain the increase. ORC at the urban stores is real but small and unquantified. Locked cases lose more margin than they save. District 4's bag checks and discipline policy suppressed shortage claims and did not cut shrink. Reinstating receiving is the preferred action. Cameras and LP officers are premature. Bag checks and chain-wide locked cases are harmful.
